title: GUI fidelity: reconcile recruitment dialog initial city and All cities selection
body:
Owner-requested GUI provenance audit by GPT-6.1 Sol at high reasoning. Potential stale implementation/default or contradictory source interpretation; not yet a confirmed original-side control.

Current remake: [RecruitUnitDialog opening selection](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/blob/4d70275aac4e155c0370a3ee23525cf34450a908/godot/UI/Dialogs/RecruitUnitDialog.cs#L304) selects All cities when OpensOnAllCities applies, otherwise the first listed city. [StrategyDialogModels](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/blob/4d70275aac4e155c0370a3ee23525cf34450a908/godot/UI/Dialogs/StrategyDialogModels.cs#L597) also starts from the first listed city. T162 established the All cities handling, so trace its existing findings before deciding whether this is deliberate design or a fidelity correction.

The [recruitment report, town-list observations](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/865755e04f107afc38cdb496669d882e2551aca6/docs/reports/2026-09-29-which-cities-may-recruit-and-troop-amounts.md) says the default is the capital or town with most units training. [G1/G8](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/865755e04f107afc38cdb496669d882e2551aca6/docs/reports/2026-10-11-g1-original-checks.md) supports membership/list order and the multiple-town All cities entry, but does not unambiguously establish the initially selected row. Reconcile those claims with the actual initialization/callback code rather than assuming the older prose is correct.

Controls: no queue; capital-only queue; noncapital-only queue; two towns with unequal queues; tied queues. Put a qualified noncapital before the capital in the list, and vary queue slot order separately from city order. Open/reopen the dialog and record selected list item, visible training rows, “Create unit at” destination, and the destination after a small accepted recruitment. Include opening after a previous manual selection to detect persistence.

Deliver exact initial-selection/tie rules and which source claims need correction. Preserve already proved eligibility, cost, debt, quality and mobilisation mechanics. Do not change owner-requested Max/full-battalion behavior or add new gameplay decisions.

Acceptance: a bounded report with code-site and runtime evidence, exact EXE identity, a reproducible control matrix, observation/inference separation and explicit untested cases. Preserve inputs and keep original bytes, screenshots and private per-save hashes outside public GitHub. No remake implementation is requested. Do not interrupt the owner's running game; coordinate native Windows runs when needed.
